10.text: Keep run/status behavior and success, failure, unavailable and stale outcomes.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] `proofline.py run` and `proofline.py status` operate with the same visible semantics and successful, failed, unavailable and stale outcomes.

10.text: Extract the small shared runtime boundary into production modules.

source_refs.quote: - Move or factor shared runtime helpers into clearly named production modules, rather than importing an S6 baseline from the supported path.

10.text: Remove supported-path dependencies on S6 or historical study coordinators.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] The supported run/check path no longer needs to import `checks/s6_baseline.py` or a historical study coordinator.

10.text: Preserve snapshots, native isolation, exact identities, receipts and cumulative budgets.

source_refs.quote: - Retain host isolation, source/candidate/check identity, stale-snapshot detection, bounded cumulative budgets, actual process receipts and distinctions between check failure and unavailable execution.

10.text: Preserve the qualified macOS/Codex path; treat portability separately.

source_refs.quote: - Keep the existing qualified macOS/Codex path working; portability is a separate hypothesis, not permission to remove safeguards.

10.text: Cover native-security and deterministic regressions; keep native qualification explicit.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Native-security and deterministic regressions cover candidate immutability, exact command matching, protected material, timeouts and resource accounting.

10.text: Keep normal CI passing on the supported matrix.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Normal CI passes on its supported test matrix; native qualification remains explicit rather than mocked into a success claim.

10.text: Explain the supported entry point in README/SKILL, preserve historical experiments, and add no compulsory model role or ceremony.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] README/SKILL explain the small supported entry point and keep historical research clearly separated.
- Keep historical `deliver`/`resume` experiments and their original evidence preserved; do not silently restore experimental certification or publication.
- [ ] No new compulsory model role, planning format, framework abstraction, or ceremony is added.

11.text: Add model-free check mode for an existing candidate and full original request.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] A coding agent can submit an existing candidate without Proofline launching Codex or any other model (assert zero model dispatches).

Introduce `proofline.py check` as a local, model-free mode accepting an existing repository/candidate, the original source request and explicit executable checks. Choose a documented, safe way to snapshot even a dirty working tree, including relevant untracked files, without deleting or modifying user work. Execute checks against an isolated frozen candidate, not a mutable live worktree. Reuse qualified sandbox, receipt, time-budget and integrity mechanisms where possible.

11.text: Snapshot dirty and relevant untracked work without changing the original repository.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] The source repository remains byte-for-byte untouched, including dirty and untracked work; no reset, stash, auto-commit, or unapproved publication.

11.text: Bind the candidate, original request and exact selected argv to evidence.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] The selected candidate, original request and exact command argument lists are bound to the record. Status detects changed or missing evidence and does not reuse stale checks.

11.text: Run selected checks on an isolated frozen candidate within the native boundary and explicit budgets.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Selected checks run on the frozen candidate in the native protected boundary with explicit budgets and without granting network access or external effects.

11.text: Separate failure, unavailability and completed passes; scope CHECKS PASSED to actual commands.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Failures, unavailable executions, and completed passes are distinct. `CHECKS PASSED` is scoped to the actual commands, never full-promise certification.

11.text: Test dirty/untracked snapshots, tampering, failure/unavailability, zero dispatch and source preservation.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Deterministic tests cover dirty worktrees, untracked files, freeze/receipt tampering, failed/unavailable checks, zero model dispatch, and source preservation.

11.text: Disclose unsupported platforms/file types; refuse unprotected fallback.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Clearly disclose any initially unsupported platforms or file types; no silent fallback to unprotected checks.

11.text: Add no correction agent, reviewer, risk scorer, automatic test generation or publication.

source_refs.quote: No correction agent, new reviewer/prover, risk scorer, PR/merge, or automatic generation of acceptance tests.

14.text: Give exact argv, exit status, elapsed time, bounded output references and candidate/source identity for each check.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] For each check, report exact argv, exit status, elapsed time, bounded stdout/stderr references, and frozen candidate/source identity.

14.text: Show supplied expected/observed values only where applicable; do not invent expectations.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] A failed behavior assertion may show supplied expected and observed values and linked outcome IDs; otherwise report the actual command failure without fabricated expectations.

14.text: Separate failed checks, missing evidence, boundary/environment unavailability, timeouts and stale receipts.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Distinguish observed check failures, missing/insufficient evidence, environment/boundary unavailability, timeouts, and stale receipts.

14.text: Give concise actionable guidance while retaining raw logs separately.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Produce concise plain-language guidance an existing coding agent can act upon; preserve logs for audit without dumping them into the primary answer.

14.text: Keep successful results short and model-free.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Successful commands produce a short result and do not trigger another reviewer or unnecessary model invocation.

14.text: Test passes/failures, missing/truncated output, timeouts, mutation attempts, bad metadata and status readback.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Tests cover failing and passing commands, truncated or missing output, timeouts, unauthorized mutation attempts, malformed expected/actual metadata, and correct status re-read.

14.text: Support optional source IDs, distinguishing actual failures from untested promises and proposed behavior; ordinary feedback stays usable without a mapping.

source_refs.quote: When optional [#13](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/13) requirement IDs/source citations are present, report the affected `R` IDs alongside actual command receipts, and distinguish **a demonstrated failing test** from **an untested promise / an unavailable check / a proposed expected behavior**. Do not invent a test expectation from a planner's wording or call a missing check a candidate defect. Without any requirements mapping or Intentline, the ordinary concise check feedback must remain fully usable. No model dispatch or peer integration belongs in the mandatory feedback path.

14.text: Add no reviewer, mandatory analysis bundle, automatic diagnosis claims or correction.

source_refs.quote: Another AI reviewer, mandatory static analysis bundle, automatic diagnosis disguised as ground truth, or auto-correction.

13.text: Keep direct check usable without a plan, Intentline/P2P, extra model, file or approval step.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] A direct check needs **no** acceptance plan, Intentline/P2P installation, second model call, additional mandatory file or approval ceremony. Existing run/check/status semantics and native sandbox/receipt integrity remain intact.

13.text: Preserve and display the full original request even without supplied rows.

source_refs.quote: Extend the supported, model-free `proofline.py check` / `status` record to accept **optional**, small caller-provided source-linked outcome rows, each with a stable ID, exact original-source citation and selected check IDs/argv associations. Preserve and display the full original request regardless of whether any rows were supplied.

13.text: Accept optional stable source-linked rows, validate source/command/candidate identities, and reject stale or contradictory claims.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Optional rows identify source-linked obligations and outcomes, including positive and negative behaviors, compatibility constraints and exceptions. Validate IDs, source identity/quoted lines, exact selected-command references and candidate binding; reject missing/stale/contradictory claims. Source text always outranks an incomplete mapping.

13.text: Report the four specified per-obligation outcomes; an unlinked promise is NOT DEMONSTRATED and green checks provide limited evidence.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Report, **per supplied obligation**, actual linked-check outcomes: `LINKED CHECKS PASSED (limited evidence)`, `CHECK FAILED`, `CHECK UNAVAILABLE`, or `NOT DEMONSTRATED`. Never call a green command proof of the full obligation or all obligations. A requirement with *no selected check* is not demonstrated, not failed.

13.text: Support optional same-agent source rereading and source-cited gap proposals, with completeness unknown if absent and no extra model.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Support an **optional step by the same existing coding agent**: reread the complete original source, compare it with the recorded rows/selected checks, and propose any apparent omitted material promise or high-value negative/compatibility case with a verbatim source citation and test suggestion. Record such findings as **proposals/gaps**, not authenticated or complete review. Proofline itself dispatches zero extra models. If no gap analysis was performed, make coverage completeness **unknown**, not silently complete.

13.text: Label agent-derived expected behavior and checks as proposals; actual success needs receipts.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Any listed expected behavior, `oracle`, or proposed check derived from an agent is explicitly a *proposed expectation*, not an independently established answer. Actual success requires executable receipts.

13.text: Cover all requested negative cases, including green tests with uncovered Unicode, stale/forged identities and omitted constraints.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Negative tests: valid green existing suite but source's Unicode promise left uncovered; missing/duplicate IDs, omitted material source quote, changed source, wrong candidate, forged command link, failed check, unavailable sandbox, stale receipt, and an advisory plan that omits a user constraint.

13.text: Keep handoffs concise and detailed identities inspectable.

source_refs.quote: - [ ] Output stays concise; detailed source/check/receipt identities are available for inspection but do not clutter ordinary successful handoffs.

13.text: Keep Intentline parsing optional and separate, and add no semantic certificate, requirement extractor, generator, reviewer, planner or publication controller.

source_refs.quote: This issue defines the **generic evidence mapping**, not a bundled Intentline parser. Follow-on **[Proofline #23](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/23)** may consume existing Intentline schema-1 `R` rows, boundaries, proposed oracles, evidence gaps and exact export identities as **optional untrusted guidance**, with no automatic adoption or peer execution. Keep source quotation and IDs compatible where straightforward; a caller-authored direct mapping remains equally supported.
No automatic semantic completeness certificate, universal requirement extraction, automatic test generator, independent AI reviewer/prover, workflow planner, or PR/merge controller.
